name: Track competitor pricing and news changes in Google Sheets with Gemini, Gmail and Slack

parameters.content:
## Track competitor pricing and news changes in Google Sheets with Gemini, Gmail and Slack

Monitor competitor websites and news automatically every week. Built for founders, marketers and sales teams, this workflow detects pricing, product and messaging changes, uses Google Gemini to rate what matters to your business, logs every change in Google Sheets and sends a short brief by Gmail and Slack.

### How it works
1. Runs every Monday at 8 AM (you can change the schedule).
2. Reads your competitor pages and last week's snapshots from Google Sheets, skipping rows marked as inactive.
3. Fetches each page, turns the HTML into clean text and compares it line by line with the last snapshot.
4. Saves each page's status and text to the Snapshots tab. If a fetch fails, the last good copy is kept, so outages are never reported as changes.
5. Sends only the changed lines to Google Gemini, which rates each change, labels it and explains why it matters. Noise is dropped and real changes go to the Change Log tab.
6. Collects each competitor's headlines from the last 7 days with Google News RSS (no API key needed).
7. Gemini writes a weekly brief with top moves, threats, opportunities and recommended actions, sent as an HTML email via Gmail and as a summary to Slack.

### Setup
1. Create a Google Sheet with three tabs and these header rows. Competitors: Competitor, Page URL, Page Type, News Keywords, Active. Snapshots: Page URL, Competitor, Page Type, Status, Last Checked, Last Changed, Content. Change Log: Date, Competitor, Page Type, Page URL, Significance, Change Type, Headline, What Changed, Why It Matters.
2. Add one row per competitor page to watch in the Competitors tab. Set Active to "no" to pause a row.
3. Open the Settings node: paste your Google Sheet URL, describe your company and what you sell, and enter the email recipients.
4. Connect Google Sheets (four nodes), Gmail (Email Brief) and a free Google Gemini API key from aistudio.google.com (both Gemini nodes).
5. Connect Slack and set your channel in Post to Slack (default #competitor-intel), or delete that node.
6. Click Execute workflow once to save a baseline, then publish the workflow so it runs every week.

### Requirements
- Google account with Google Sheets and Gmail
- Google Gemini API key (the free tier works for weekly runs)
- Slack workspace (optional)

### Customization
- Change the schedule in the Every Monday 8 AM node. Daily works well for pricing pages.
- Edit the significance rules in the AI Change Analyst prompt to match your market.
- Use the News Keywords column (for example "Notion" software) when a competitor has a common name.
- Replace Fetch Page with a scraping API such as Firecrawl for sites that load content with JavaScript.
- Swap Gemini for another model by replacing the two Gemini chat model nodes.

### Additional info
- The first run only saves a baseline. Change reports start from the second run; news is included from the first run.
- Only the changed lines of each page are sent to the AI, so a weekly run needs very few AI calls. If you hit the Gemini free tier's daily limit, pick another Flash model in the Gemini nodes or enable billing.
- Only monitor public pages, and respect each website's terms of use.

### 1. Load settings & competitor list
Edit **Settings** once. The competitor list and last week's snapshots are read from your Google Sheet. Rows with Active set to "no" are skipped.

### 2. Detect website changes
- Pages are fetched 3 at a time and cleaned into plain text.
- Each page is compared line by line with its last snapshot.
- Every page's status is saved to the **Snapshots** tab.
- A failed fetch keeps the old copy, so outages never look like changes.

### 3. AI Change Analyst
Only changed pages reach the AI, and only the added and removed lines are sent. Gemini rates each change and explains the business impact. Changes rated *noise* are dropped. The rest are saved to **Change Log** and passed to the brief.

### 4. News monitoring
Google News RSS for each competitor (last 7 days, free, no API key). Use the *News Keywords* column to avoid mix-ups with companies that share a common name.

### 5. Weekly brief & delivery
All results are merged into one research pack. One AI call writes the brief, which is rendered as a clean HTML email and a short Slack summary.

messageValues.message:
=You are a competitive intelligence analyst working for {{ $('Settings').first().json.your_company }}.
What we sell: {{ $('Settings').first().json.your_offer }}

You receive the lines of text that were removed from and added to a competitor's web page since the last check. Work out what actually changed and whether it matters to us.

significance:
- high: price or plan changes, new product or major feature, free tier or trial changes, new target market, major repositioning
- medium: notable feature updates, new integrations, big-name customer logos or case studies, discounts and promotions, clear messaging changes
- low: minor copy edits, small wording tweaks, new blog teasers
- noise: dates, counters, cookie banners, rotating testimonials, reordered content, tracking text, or anything with no business meaning

Rules:
- Only describe what is in the diff. Never guess numbers or facts that are not shown.
- Quote exact prices and plan names when they changed, e.g. "Pro plan: $49 -> $59/month".
- headline: max 12 words.
- what_changed: 1-2 plain sentences.
- why_it_matters: one sentence on how this could affect our sales, pricing or positioning.

=You are the head of competitive intelligence at {{ $('Settings').first().json.your_company }}.
What we sell: {{ $('Settings').first().json.your_offer }}

Turn the research into a brief a busy founder can read in two minutes.
- Use only facts from the research. Never invent competitors, numbers, launches or dates.
- Ignore headlines that are clearly about a different company or topic with the same name.
- subject: a specific email subject line under 80 characters that names the biggest move.
- executive_summary: 2-3 sentences on what matters most this week. If nothing important happened, say so plainly.
- top_moves: up to 5 of the most important competitor moves, most important first.
- threats and opportunities: up to 3 each, concrete and tied to the research. Empty lists are fine.
- recommended_actions: up to 3 specific actions for our team this week, e.g. "Update our comparison page: Acme now charges $59 for Pro".
- If every page is a new baseline, explain that monitoring has started and next week's brief will show website changes.
